messages.author: 5ac06d2d2fd9d206
messages.subject: simulateData for sem
parts:
Hello,
I have simulated a dataset based on this code: 
mymodel =' # measurement model
 var1 =~ x1 + 0.744*x2 + 0.744*x3 + 0.744*x4
 var2 =~ x5 + 0.782*x6 + 0.782*x7 + 0.782*x8 + 0.782*x9
 var3 =~ x10 + 0.863*x11 + 0.863*x12 + 0.863*x13 + 0.863*x14
 var4 =~ x15 + 0.818*x16 + 0.818*x18 + 0.818*x17 + 0.818*x19 + 0.818*x20
 # structural model var1 ~ var2*0.564
 var3 ~ var2*0.461 + var1*0.402
 var4 ~ var3*0.636 + var2*0.224 + var1*0.056' 
 #Simulation
 mydata = simulateData(model=mymodel, model.type = "sem", sample.nobs=200)
When I now calculate a sem based on the model (so same model without the path coefficients), I get a model with very good fit but the path coefficients are not 0.564 etc. or even similar to that. What did I do wrong?

messages.author: f6d12b388faad456
messages.subject: Re: simulateData for sem
parts:
Hi,

The var1 ~ var2*0.564 part is in the same line as the # symbol. So, it is being treated as a commentary, not as a part of the model.

Best,
Yago

​

messages.author: 5ac06d2d2fd9d206
messages.subject: Re: simulateData for sem
parts: For future reference: I figured it out. The problem was that I wrote e.g. var2*0.461, however, it only works when you write 0.461*var2
